newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House approves $95 billion tax cut bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House approves $95 billion tax cut bill.

text.p: The U.S. House of Representatives on Thursday approved a five-year, $95 billion net tax-cut package that would give Americans the first major tax reduction in 16 years.
The legislation includes a $500-per-child tax credit, tax breaks for higher education, a capital gains tax cut, inheritance tax relief and expanded Individual Retirement Accounts.
The House voted 389-43 to approve overwhelmingly the tax cut bill, which emerged after a May budget agreement between congressional leaders and the White House.
The bill would raise about $56 billion over five years in revenues from aviation taxes and international passenger fees, a cigarette tax increase, and closing of some corporate loopholes.
The Senate continued debating the tax bill and may not vote on it until Friday. The House and Senate have approved companion spending legislation.
"We're just warming up," House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, a Texas Republican, said. "There are more taxes to be cut."
